items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Willie Humphrey was saying how many guys were from here like Simeon and Al Wynn and they didn't play anything down here.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. One fellow I wanna ask you, maybe you don't know, but the seems that I never asked him, it seems like he's from here, but I hear a lot of people talking about him, but Al Wynn, is he from New Orleans? Yeah?

Yeah, but I don't think he played down here. We were talking about that, Willie Humphrey was saying how many guys were from here like Simeon and Al Wynn and they didn't play anything down here. Uh-huh. Preston Jackson, you know.
I'm sure I didn't think I was, you know, why nobody said he played around here?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Yeah, then after I heard he had Willie Humphreys a while.

ctx.x: He had Willard Toomey at one time, did you know him?
Yeah, then after I heard he had Willie Humphreys a while.
Yeah, and let me see, there was another one I can't think of. Well, let's see, Paul Barnes I think played clarinet. Yeah.
And they had another bad man, Willie Umford's brother, Earl Umford. He was bad.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: And I got a little lesson from Willie Humphrey's daddy too.

ctx.x: I could just whistle something up and pick the horn up and blow it. I don't know what key I was on unless I knew I played. And, uh, who taught you how to read it? Well, I liked something in the Army. I stole my reading. That's the truth I stole. A fella named Chip used to be there. Yeah, he did. Now, you heard of him. His name was Lewis Mathis. He was one of his kid over at trumpet players way back years ago and called him Chip. Well, I was in the Army and I used to go on watching him. I had my music up there but…
He's daddy, huh? Which, no, which Willie Humphrey? I mean there's a- The old man. Not Willie Humphrey would play the clarinet.
